steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The EU began as the European Coal and Steel Community in 1951 and evolved into a political and economic union of 27 member states cooperating on trade, law, and policy.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The UK joined the European Communities in 1973. A 1975 referendum confirmed membership with 67% voting to stay in. Membership gave access to the single market and freedom of movement.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The 2016 EU referendum result: 51.9% voted Leave, 48.1% voted Remain. Turnout was 72.2%. England and Wales voted Leave; Scotland and Northern Ireland voted Remain.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Key Leave arguments: regaining parliamentary sovereignty (making all UK laws in the UK), controlling immigration (ending freedom of movement), making independent trade deals, and saving EU budget contributions (£17.4bn gross in 2019).

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always present both sides of the Brexit debate — it was closely divided (51.9% vs 48.1%) Distinguish between the EU (27 member states) and Europe (geographic continent) — they are not the same Use correct terminology: 'single market' not 'common market', 'freedom of movement' not 'open borders'
